[[File:Xuong tree.svg|thumb|upright=1.2|A Xuong tree. Only one component of the non-tree edges (the red component) has an odd number of edges, the minimum possible for this graph.]]
In [[graph theory]], a '''Xuong tree''' is a [[spanning tree]] <math>T</math> of a given graph <math>G</math> with the property that, in the remaining graph <math>G-T</math>, the number of [[Connected component (graph theory)|connected components]] with an odd number of edges is as small as possible.{{r|bw}}
They are named after Nguyen Huy Xuong, who used them to characterize the [[graph embedding|cellular embeddings]] of a given graph having the largest possible [[Genus (mathematics)|genus]].{{r|x}}

According to Xuong's results, if <math>T</math> is a Xuong tree
and the numbers of edges in the components of <math>G-T</math> are <math>m_1,m_2,\dots, m_k</math>, then the maximum genus of an embedding of <math>G</math> is <math>\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^k\lfloor m_i/2\rfloor</math>.{{r|bw|x}}
Any one of these components, having <math>m_i</math> edges, can be partitioned into <math>\lfloor m_i/2\rfloor</math> edge-disjoint two-edge paths, with possibly one additional left-over edge.{{r|s}}
An embedding of maximum genus may be obtained from a planar embedding of the Xuong tree by adding each two-edge path to the embedding in such a way that it increases the genus by one.{{r|bw|x}}

A Xuong tree, and a maximum-genus embedding derived from it, may be found in any graph in [[polynomial time]], by a transformation to a more general computational problem on [[matroid]]s, the [[matroid parity problem]] for [[linear matroid]]s.{{r|bw|fgm}}
